title: Provider Router - Go LiteLLM Implementation
description: Core provider-agnostic routing layer. Reimplements LiteLLM concepts in Go: unified OpenAI-compatible interface, provider adapters, load balancing, fallbacks, cost tracking. This is the foundation that decouples agent orchestration from any specific LLM provider.

title: Implement Google Gemini provider adapter
description: Adapter for Google Gemini/Vertex AI. Handle auth (API key or service account), streaming, tool use translation.

title: Build router with model-to-provider mapping
description: Router that reads config and routes model requests to correct provider adapter. Support model aliases (e.g., 'supervisor' -> 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514').

title: Add fallback chain support to router
description: When primary model/provider fails, automatically try fallback models. Configurable fallback chains per role. Error classification (rate limit, context window, auth, timeout).

title: Add load balancing to router
description: Distribute requests across multiple deployments of same model. Strategies: round-robin, least-busy, latency-based. Health checking with cooldown.

title: Add cost tracking to router
description: Track token usage and estimated cost per request, per model, per role. Price tables for known models. Budget limits per role/session.

title: Analyze gastown source for Claude Code coupling points
description: Map every file/function in gastown that references Claude Code, Anthropic, or hardcoded provider assumptions. Produce a coupling report for surgical replacement.

title: Abstract agent session layer from Claude Code
description: Gastown's session layer manages Claude Code instances via settings.json hooks. Replace with generic agent session that launches any LLM-backed agent via the provider router.

title: Implement generic agent launcher (replace Claude Code spawning)
description: Replace gastown's Claude Code tmux session spawning with a generic agent launcher that starts an LLM session via the provider router. Support both interactive and non-interactive modes.

title: Adapt polecat lifecycle for multi-provider
description: Ensure polecat identity/session/sandbox layers work with any provider. Model assignment per polecat configurable. Idle/working/stalled states provider-agnostic.

title: Adapt Mayor role for configurable supervisor model
description: Mayor currently assumes Claude. Make supervisor model configurable — any frontier model can be Mayor. Preserve convoy creation and work decomposition patterns.

title: et nodes subcommand
description: New subcommand that pings each Ollama provider in config, lists reachable nodes with model names and a quick token rate benchmark. Shows offline nodes clearly. Pattern: et nodes [--config path]

title: Research: testing models suitable for the tester role
description: Research and evaluate LLM models well-suited for the tester role (code validation, output testing). Key requirement: should NOT be the same model that generated the code being tested — diversity reduces blind spots. Evaluate: DeepSeek-R1 variants, Qwen3-Coder (different size from workers), Gemini Flash, Mistral Devstral. Consider open-weight models deployable on ai01/phoenix so the tester is fully local and free.
acceptance_criteria: Shortlist of 3-5 models with rationale; recommended default for tester role in config; note on why model diversity matters for testing

title: Research: reviewer models for output quality scoring
description: Research models suited for the reviewer role (code review, quality scoring, flag low-quality outputs). Should differ from the worker pool models. Consider: reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1, QwQ), instruction-tuned review specialists, or small fast models for lightweight flagging. Evaluate cost/speed tradeoffs — reviewer runs once per worker result.
acceptance_criteria: Shortlist of 3-5 models with rationale; recommended default for reviewer role; latency/cost estimate per review

title: LM Studio Provider Support
description: Add LM Studio as a first-class provider in et. LM Studio exposes an OpenAI-compatible API on a configurable network interface, so this leverages the existing OpenAI provider adapter with additions for model discovery, health checks, and network interface binding. Branch: feature/lm-studio-provider, PR to main.
acceptance_criteria: LM Studio instances configurable in YAML, model auto-discovery works, health checks pass, et run works against LM Studio endpoints.

title: Define LM Studio provider type in config schema
description: Add 'lmstudio' as a recognized provider type in provider/config.go. LM Studio uses OpenAI-compatible chat completions API, so this extends the existing openai provider type with lmstudio-specific defaults (default port 1234, no auth required by default). Add config validation for lmstudio type.
acceptance_criteria: Provider type 'lmstudio' accepted in YAML config, validates correctly, reuses OpenAI adapter internally.

title: Agent Orchestrator - Gastown Fork Adaptation
description: Fork and adapt gastown's multi-agent orchestration (Mayor, Polecats, Crew, Witness, Refinery) to use the Provider Router instead of Claude Code. Replace hooks-based Claude Code integration with generic provider interface. Preserve gastown's work decomposition patterns (convoys, beads, worktrees).

title: Adapt Witness and Refinery for generic agents
description: Ensure monitoring (Witness) and merge queue (Refinery) roles work with provider-agnostic agent sessions.

title: Implement LM Studio model discovery API
description: LM Studio exposes GET /v1/models listing all loaded models. Implement a discovery function that queries this endpoint and returns available models. This enables 'et models' to show LM Studio models alongside other providers. Handle the case where LM Studio has no models loaded (empty response).
acceptance_criteria: 'et models' shows LM Studio models when lmstudio provider is configured, handles empty model list gracefully.

title: Add LM Studio health check endpoint
description: Implement health check for LM Studio instances by hitting GET /v1/models (or a lightweight endpoint). Integrate with 'et nodes' to show LM Studio instance status. Consider that LM Studio may be running but with no models loaded (healthy but idle).
acceptance_criteria: 'et nodes' shows LM Studio status (up/down/idle), health check distinguishes running-with-models vs running-without-models.

title: Network interface binding for LM Studio instances
description: LM Studio can bind to specific network interfaces (0.0.0.0 vs 127.0.0.1 vs specific IP). Document and validate in config that the base_url points to the correct network interface. Add a config example showing multiple LM Studio instances on different hosts/interfaces.
acceptance_criteria: Config example in electrictown.yaml.example shows LM Studio on multiple interfaces, validation warns if localhost-only instance is referenced from remote pool.

title: LM Studio provider integration tests
description: Add integration tests for the LM Studio provider path. Test config parsing with lmstudio type, model discovery response parsing, health check response handling. Use httptest for mock LM Studio API responses.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover config parsing, model discovery, health check, and error cases. All pass.

title: LM Studio documentation and example config
description: Update README.md and electrictown.yaml.example with LM Studio provider configuration examples. Document the lmstudio provider type, model discovery, and multi-instance setup.
acceptance_criteria: README has LM Studio section, example config includes commented lmstudio provider block.

title: Agent Backend Core Infrastructure
description: Build the foundational abstraction for routing et roles to CLI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Aider, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Gemini CLI) instead of LLM API providers. Agents are processes with side effects (file changes), not chat completion APIs. This epic defines the AgentBackend interface, agent session lifecycle, output normalization, config schema, and role-to-agent routing. All individual agent adapter epics depend on this. Branch: feature/agent-backend-core, PR to main.
acceptance_criteria: AgentBackend interface defined, config schema supports agents section, role routing can dispatch to agents, output normalization produces uniform AgentResult structs.

title: Define AgentBackend interface
description: Create internal/agent/backend.go with the AgentBackend interface. Unlike Provider (send text, receive text via HTTP), AgentBackend models process lifecycle: Execute(ctx, task AgentTask) -> AgentResult. AgentTask contains prompt, working directory, environment, and timeout. AgentResult contains stdout text, stderr text, file changes ([]FileChange), exit code, and duration. This is the contract all agent adapters implement.
acceptance_criteria: AgentBackend interface defined with Execute method, AgentTask and AgentResult structs defined, FileChange struct captures path + diff/content.

title: Agent session lifecycle management
description: Implement agent process lifecycle in internal/agent/session.go. Spawn agent CLI process, feed task via stdin or --prompt flag, monitor for timeout/hang, collect stdout/stderr, detect exit code. Handle graceful shutdown (SIGTERM then SIGKILL after timeout). Support both one-shot (run and exit) and persistent (long-running with task injection) modes.
acceptance_criteria: Session can spawn a process, feed input, collect output, enforce timeout, handle graceful shutdown. Both one-shot and persistent modes work.

title: Agent output normalization layer
description: Create internal/agent/normalize.go with output normalization. Each agent adapter provides a Normalizer that parses agent-specific output into the common AgentResult struct. The normalizer extracts: prose output (explanations), file changes (diffs or full content), error messages, and structured metadata. Define the Normalizer interface that adapters implement.
acceptance_criteria: Normalizer interface defined, base implementation handles common patterns (diff output, file markers), adapters can extend with agent-specific parsing.

title: Config schema for agents section in YAML
description: Extend provider/config.go to add a top-level 'agents:' section to the YAML config. Each agent entry has: type (claude-code, codex, aider, opencode, openclaw, gemini-cli), transport (local, ssh), host (for ssh), command (CLI binary path), flags (default CLI flags), working_dir, env (environment variables), timeout. Add validation for agent configs. Agent names must not conflict with provider names or built-in role names.
acceptance_criteria: Config parses agents section with dedicated model field, validates type/transport/host, model field automatically maps to agent --model flag, rejects conflicts with provider/role names, resolves env vars like providers do.
notes: UPDATED: Agent config must include a first-class 'model' field (not buried in generic flags). The model field specifies which model the agent CLI should use (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-20250514 for Claude Code, o4-mini for Codex, gpt-4o for Aider, provider/model for OpenCode). et automatically maps this to the agent's --model flag during execution. This keeps agent model selection consistent with how et handles model routing for LLM providers.

title: Design YAML config schema for model routing
description: Config format mapping: roles -> models -> providers. Support aliases, fallbacks, per-role overrides. Example: mayor: {model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514, provider: anthropic}, polecat: {model: qwen3-coder:32b, provider: ollama-local}.

title: Role-to-agent routing in orchestration
description: Extend RoleConfig to support an 'agent:' field alongside the existing 'model:' field. A role targets either a model (LLM API) or an agent (CLI tool), never both. Update the orchestration pipeline (mayor decompose -> workers execute) to detect agent-targeted roles and dispatch via AgentBackend instead of Provider. The mayor role must always be an LLM (agents cannot decompose tasks). Worker/specialist roles can be agents.
acceptance_criteria: RoleConfig accepts agent field, validation rejects role with both model and agent, orchestrator dispatches to AgentBackend for agent roles, mayor role rejects agent assignment.

title: Agent health check and status reporting
description: Implement health checking for configured agents. For local agents: verify the CLI binary exists and is executable (which/command -v). For SSH agents: verify SSH connectivity and remote binary existence. Integrate with 'et nodes' to show agent status alongside provider status.
acceptance_criteria: 'et nodes' shows agent status (available/unavailable/unreachable), local checks verify binary, SSH checks verify connectivity + binary.

title: Agent backend unit tests
description: Comprehensive unit tests for the agent backend core: AgentBackend interface compliance, session lifecycle (spawn, timeout, shutdown), output normalization, config parsing with agents section, role-to-agent routing logic.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover interface compliance, lifecycle edge cases, normalization parsing, config validation, routing dispatch. All pass.

title: SSH Remote Agent Transport
description: Implement SSH transport layer for accessing coding agents on remote machines. et needs to spawn and manage agent processes on remote hosts via SSH. This enables routing tasks to differently-configured agent instances across the network (e.g., Claude Code on a dev server, Aider on a GPU box). Depends on Agent Backend Core (ET-96). Branch: feature/ssh-remote-transport, PR to main.
acceptance_criteria: SSH transport connects to remote hosts, spawns agent processes, collects output, handles auth and multiplexing, integrates with AgentBackend interface.

title: SSH connection manager
description: Create internal/agent/transport/ssh.go with SSH connection management. Use golang.org/x/crypto/ssh for connections. Support key-based auth (default), ssh-agent forwarding, and configurable known_hosts. Implement connection pooling to reuse SSH sessions across multiple agent invocations to the same host. Handle connection failures with retry and backoff.
acceptance_criteria: SSH connections established with key auth, ssh-agent, or explicit key file. Connection pooling reuses sessions. Retry on transient failures.

title: SSH key and authentication handling
description: Implement SSH authentication in internal/agent/transport/auth.go. Support: default key (~/.ssh/id_ed25519, id_rsa), explicit key path in config, ssh-agent socket, and passphrase-protected keys (prompt or env var). Config fields: ssh_key, ssh_user, ssh_port (default 22). Follow OpenSSH config conventions where possible.
acceptance_criteria: Auth works with default keys, explicit keys, ssh-agent. Config supports ssh_key/ssh_user/ssh_port fields. Passphrase keys handled.

title: Remote agent process spawning via SSH
description: Implement remote process spawning over SSH in internal/agent/transport/remote.go. Given an SSH session and agent config, spawn the agent CLI on the remote host with the correct command, flags, environment, and working directory. Pipe task input via stdin, collect stdout/stderr. Handle the remote process lifecycle (start, monitor, timeout, kill).
acceptance_criteria: Agent process spawned on remote host via SSH, input piped, output collected, timeout enforced, process killed on timeout.

title: SSH session multiplexing
description: Implement SSH session multiplexing so multiple concurrent agent tasks to the same host share one TCP connection but have independent sessions/channels. This is critical for pool parallelism - running 4 agents on the same remote host should not open 4 TCP connections. Use golang.org/x/crypto/ssh built-in channel multiplexing.
acceptance_criteria: Multiple concurrent agent tasks to same host use single TCP connection, each with independent channel. Pool of 4 agents to same host verified.

title: Remote agent discovery
description: Implement a discovery command that detects which coding agents are installed on a remote host. SSH to the host and check for each supported agent binary (claude, codex, aider, opencode, openclaw, gemini). Report versions where available. This helps users configure their agents section.
acceptance_criteria: 'et nodes --discover' (or similar) SSHs to configured hosts and reports which agent CLIs are available and their versions.

title: SSH transport integration tests
description: Integration tests for SSH transport. Test connection establishment, authentication methods, remote process spawning, output collection, timeout handling, session multiplexing. Use testcontainers or a local SSH server for testing.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover connection, auth, spawning, output, timeout, multiplexing. All pass.

title: Implement config parser and validator
description: Go config parser for the YAML schema. Validate model/provider combinations. Error on invalid configs before launching agents.

title: Claude Code Agent Adapter
description: Implement the AgentBackend adapter for Anthropic Claude Code CLI. Claude Code supports non-interactive mode via --prompt flag (or piped stdin in non-TTY). Priority adapter since et is already in the Claude ecosystem. Depends on Agent Backend Core (ET-96) and SSH Remote Transport (ET-104). Branch: feature/agent-claude-code, PR to main.
acceptance_criteria: Claude Code adapter implements AgentBackend, works locally and via SSH, output normalized to AgentResult, configurable in agents section.

title: Claude Code CLI detection and version check
description: Implement Claude Code detection in internal/agent/adapters/claudecode/detect.go. Check for 'claude' binary in PATH, verify it is Claude Code (not another claude binary), get version. Handle the case where Claude Code is installed but not authenticated.
acceptance_criteria: Detection finds claude binary, confirms it is Claude Code via version output, reports auth status.

title: Claude Code --prompt mode integration
description: Implement the core Execute method for Claude Code adapter. Use 'claude --prompt task' for non-interactive one-shot execution. Configure via agent config flags (--model, --max-turns, --allowedTools). Handle Claude Code output format (markdown with tool use blocks). Set appropriate timeout for long-running coding tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Execute sends task via --prompt, collects full output, respects timeout, passes configured flags.

title: Claude Code output parsing and normalization
description: Implement the Normalizer for Claude Code output. Parse Claude Code markdown output to extract: prose explanation, file changes (from Edit/Write tool calls), command outputs, and error messages. Map to AgentResult struct.
acceptance_criteria: Normalizer extracts prose, file changes, errors from Claude Code output. Handles tool use blocks and markdown formatting.

title: Claude Code adapter tests
description: Unit tests for Claude Code adapter. Test detection logic, --prompt flag construction, output parsing/normalization, error handling (auth failures, timeout, binary not found).
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover detection, execution, normalization, error cases. All pass.

title: Codex CLI Agent Adapter
description: Implement the AgentBackend adapter for OpenAI Codex CLI. Codex supports 'codex exec' for one-shot execution and --full-auto for autonomous mode. Note known instability in non-TTY environments (open issues #4219, #3820). Depends on Agent Backend Core (ET-96) and SSH Remote Transport (ET-104). Branch: feature/agent-codex, PR to main.
acceptance_criteria: Codex adapter implements AgentBackend, handles exec mode, output normalized, known headless issues documented and mitigated.

title: Codex CLI detection and setup validation
description: Implement Codex detection in internal/agent/adapters/codex/detect.go. Check for 'codex' binary, get version, verify authentication status (OPENAI_API_KEY or codex login). Warn about known non-TTY instability.
acceptance_criteria: Detection finds codex binary, reports version and auth status, warns about headless issues.

title: Codex exec mode integration
description: Implement Execute method using 'codex exec task' for one-shot execution. Support --json flag for structured output. Handle the known panics in non-TTY by wrapping in pseudo-TTY if needed (using script or expect). Configure via agent config flags (--model, --full-auto).
acceptance_criteria: Execute works via codex exec, JSON output parsed when available, pseudo-TTY fallback for non-TTY issues.

title: Codex output parsing and normalization
description: Implement Normalizer for Codex output. Parse both plain text and JSON output modes. Extract file changes, explanations, and error messages. Handle the case where Codex crashes mid-execution (partial output recovery).
acceptance_criteria: Normalizer handles text and JSON output, extracts file changes, recovers from partial output.

title: Codex adapter tests
description: Unit tests for Codex adapter. Test detection, exec mode, output parsing, error handling, pseudo-TTY fallback logic.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover detection, execution, normalization, error cases. All pass.

title: Build et CLI entry point (adapt gt)
description: Rename/adapt gastown's gt CLI to et (electrictown). Preserve core commands: sling, done, prime, mail. Add provider-specific commands: et models, et providers, et route.

title: Aider Agent Adapter
description: Implement the AgentBackend adapter for aider-chat Aider CLI. Aider has strong headless support via --message and --yes flags, with git integration for tracking changes. Python-based (pip install aider-chat). Depends on Agent Backend Core (ET-96) and SSH Remote Transport (ET-104). Branch: feature/agent-aider, PR to main.
acceptance_criteria: Aider adapter implements AgentBackend, uses --message --yes mode, git changes tracked, output normalized.

title: Aider CLI detection and config
description: Implement Aider detection in internal/agent/adapters/aider/detect.go. Check for 'aider' binary (Python package), get version, verify LLM API key configuration (Aider uses its own model config). Support configuring Aider model choice via et agent config.
acceptance_criteria: Detection finds aider binary, reports version, validates API key availability for configured model.

title: Aider --message --yes mode integration
description: Implement Execute method using 'aider --message task --yes' for non-interactive execution. Support --auto-commits for git integration. Configure model via --model flag. Handle --message-file for long prompts. Set working directory to the target codebase.
acceptance_criteria: Execute works via --message --yes, auto-commits optional, model configurable, long prompts handled via temp file.

title: Aider output parsing and normalization
description: Implement Normalizer for Aider output. Parse Aider terminal output to extract: file edit blocks, git commit messages, error messages. Aider uses search/replace blocks in output - parse these into FileChange structs.
acceptance_criteria: Normalizer extracts file edits, commit messages, errors from Aider output. Search/replace blocks parsed correctly.

title: Aider adapter tests
description: Unit tests for Aider adapter. Test detection, --message mode, output parsing, git integration, error handling.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover detection, execution, normalization, git, error cases. All pass.

title: OpenCode Agent Adapter
description: Implement the AgentBackend adapter for OpenCode (opencode.ai). OpenCode is Go-based with the strongest headless story of all agents - supports 'opencode run' for one-shot, 'opencode serve' for persistent server mode, and quiet mode for scripting. 120k+ GitHub stars, 75+ provider support. Depends on Agent Backend Core (ET-96) and SSH Remote Transport (ET-104). Branch: feature/agent-opencode, PR to main.
acceptance_criteria: OpenCode adapter implements AgentBackend, supports both run and serve modes, output normalized.

title: OpenCode CLI detection and setup
description: Implement OpenCode detection in internal/agent/adapters/opencode/detect.go. Check for 'opencode' binary, get version. OpenCode is Go-based like et - consider whether the serve mode (HTTP) could be used as an alternative transport to SSH for remote instances.
acceptance_criteria: Detection finds opencode binary, reports version, identifies serve mode availability.

title: OpenCode run mode integration
description: Implement Execute method using 'opencode run --model model task' for one-shot execution. Support -q (quiet) flag for script-friendly output. Configure provider/model via agent config flags.
acceptance_criteria: Execute works via opencode run, quiet mode supported, model configurable via config.

title: OpenCode serve mode integration
description: Implement an alternative transport using OpenCode 'opencode serve' HTTP server mode. This enables remote access without SSH - connect to a running OpenCode server via HTTP. Use 'opencode run --attach http://host:port task' for remote execution. This is a unique capability among the agent adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Serve mode transport connects to remote OpenCode server, tasks submitted via --attach, output collected.

title: OpenCode output parsing and normalization
description: Implement Normalizer for OpenCode output. Parse both standard and quiet mode output. Extract file changes, explanations, and errors.
acceptance_criteria: Normalizer handles both output modes, extracts file changes and prose.

title: Replace go-openai with native OpenAI HTTP client
description: Remove sashabaranov/go-openai dependency. Implement native HTTP client for OpenAI API with SSE streaming. Only external dep should be net/http.

title: OpenCode adapter tests
description: Unit tests for OpenCode adapter. Test detection, run mode, serve mode transport, output parsing, error handling.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover all modes, normalization, error cases. All pass.

title: OpenClaw Agent Adapter
description: Implement the AgentBackend adapter for OpenClaw. Note that OpenClaw is architecturally different from other agents - it is a self-hosted agent runtime and message router (gateway), not a terminal coding agent. Its coding capability is a skill/plugin, not its core function. The adapter approach may differ significantly from the other adapters. Depends on Agent Backend Core (ET-96) and SSH Remote Transport (ET-104). Branch: feature/agent-openclaw, PR to main.
acceptance_criteria: OpenClaw adapter implements AgentBackend, interfaces with OpenClaw coding skill, output normalized.

title: OpenClaw architecture analysis and adapter design
description: Analyze OpenClaw architecture to determine the best integration strategy. OpenClaw is a daemon-based gateway, not a CLI coding tool. Options: (1) interact with the coding skill via OpenClaw API, (2) spawn openclaw with a coding-specific config, (3) treat it as an HTTP backend rather than CLI process. Produce a design document before implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Design document explains integration approach, rationale, and trade-offs. Approved before implementation proceeds.

title: OpenClaw coding skill integration
description: Implement Execute method based on the design from the architecture analysis. Interface with OpenClaw coding skill to submit tasks and collect results. Handle OpenClaw daemon lifecycle (start if not running, or connect to existing).
acceptance_criteria: Execute submits coding tasks to OpenClaw, collects results, handles daemon lifecycle.

title: OpenClaw output parsing and normalization
description: Implement Normalizer for OpenClaw output. Parse the coding skill output format to extract file changes and explanations.
acceptance_criteria: Normalizer extracts file changes and prose from OpenClaw coding skill output.

title: OpenClaw adapter tests
description: Unit tests for OpenClaw adapter. Test daemon interaction, coding skill execution, output parsing, error handling.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover daemon interaction, execution, normalization, error cases. All pass.

title: Gemini CLI Agent Adapter
description: Implement the AgentBackend adapter for Google Gemini CLI. Gemini CLI supports non-interactive mode via -p/--prompt flag with JSON output (--output-format json). Free tier with generous limits (60 req/min, 1000/day). Google direct competitor to Claude Code. Depends on Agent Backend Core (ET-96) and SSH Remote Transport (ET-104). Branch: feature/agent-gemini-cli, PR to main.
acceptance_criteria: Gemini CLI adapter implements AgentBackend, uses --prompt mode with JSON output, output normalized.

title: Gemini CLI detection and auth validation
description: Implement Gemini CLI detection in internal/agent/adapters/geminicli/detect.go. Check for 'gemini' binary, get version. Validate Google auth (Gemini CLI uses Google account auth). Report free tier vs paid status.
acceptance_criteria: Detection finds gemini binary, reports version, validates auth status, identifies tier.

title: Gemini CLI --prompt mode integration
description: Implement Execute method using 'gemini -p task' for non-interactive execution. Use --output-format json for structured output. Configure via agent config flags. Handle Gemini CLI built-in tools (Google Search, file ops, shell commands).
acceptance_criteria: Execute works via -p flag, JSON output parsed, configured flags passed through.

title: Gemini CLI output parsing and normalization
description: Implement Normalizer for Gemini CLI output. Parse JSON output format to extract file changes, explanations, tool use results, and errors. Fall back to text parsing if JSON unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Normalizer handles JSON and text output, extracts file changes and prose.

title: Replace ollama/api with native Ollama HTTP client
description: Remove ollama/api dependency. Implement native HTTP client for Ollama REST API. Same API works for local and cloud.

title: Gemini CLI adapter tests
description: Unit tests for Gemini CLI adapter. Test detection, --prompt mode, JSON output parsing, text fallback, error handling.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover detection, execution, normalization, error cases. All pass.

title: et loop — Ralph Wiggum Unattended Task Runner
description: Add an 'et loop' subcommand (or --loop flag) that implements the Ralph Wiggum pattern natively in et. Reads tickets from bd (beads), iterates with fresh context per cycle, uses a loop-specific et config for cost control (local Ollama workers + selective cloud fallback). Each iteration: read next unblocked ticket from bd ready, execute via et run, verify (go test/go build), commit on success, mark ticket done, restart. Supports --epic flag to scope to one epic, --max-iterations safety cap, skip-and-flag after N failures per ticket, and notification on epic completion. Depends on Agent Backend Core (ET-205). Branch: feature/et-loop, PR to main.
acceptance_criteria: et loop subcommand exists, reads from bd ready, iterates with fresh context, uses configurable et config, respects dependency chain, enforces max iterations, skips failing tickets after N retries, notifies on completion.

title: Design et loop subcommand CLI interface
description: Design the CLI interface for et loop. Flags: --config (loop-specific YAML), --epic ET-XXX (scope to one epic), --max-iterations N (safety cap, default 20), --max-retries N (per-ticket retry limit, default 3), --cooldown Ns (delay between iterations for rate limiting), --dry-run (show what would run without executing), --notify (notification on completion/failure). Define how et loop reads from bd ready and passes ticket context to et run.
acceptance_criteria: CLI flags defined, help text written, argument parsing implemented in cmd/et/main.go.

title: Implement loop iteration engine
description: Implement the core loop in internal/loop/runner.go. Each iteration: call bd ready to get next unblocked ticket, extract ticket description and acceptance criteria, construct et run invocation with the loop config, execute, collect exit code and output. Track per-ticket attempt counts. Skip ticket after max retries and log failure. Exit loop when bd ready returns empty or max iterations reached.
acceptance_criteria: Loop engine iterates, reads from bd, executes et run per ticket, tracks retries, respects max iterations, exits cleanly.

title: Integrate bd (beads) ticket reader
description: Implement bd integration in internal/loop/tickets.go. Shell out to bd ready --json to get unblocked tickets. Parse JSON output into Go structs. Support --epic flag filtering (only return tickets belonging to a specific epic). Extract ticket title, description, acceptance criteria, and priority for prompt construction.
acceptance_criteria: Reads bd ready output, parses JSON, filters by epic, extracts all ticket fields needed for prompt construction.

title: Build loop prompt template system
description: Create the prompt template that gets passed to et run each iteration. Template includes: ticket title and description, acceptance criteria, repo context (CLAUDE.md, relevant source files), instruction to implement ONE ticket only, instruction to run go test and go build, instruction to commit on success. Support customizable prompt templates via --template flag.
acceptance_criteria: Prompt template produces well-structured prompts, includes ticket context and verification instructions, customizable via flag.

title: Implement verification and commit gate
description: After each et run iteration, verify the work: run go build and go test. If both pass, create a git commit with the ticket ID in the message and call bd close on the ticket. If either fails, increment the retry counter for that ticket and move on. Log all verification results for post-run review.
acceptance_criteria: Verification runs go build + go test, commits on success with ticket ID, closes ticket in bd, retries on failure, logs all results.

title: Add notification and reporting
description: Implement notifications for loop events. Use the existing PAI voice notification endpoint (localhost:8888/notify) for: loop start, epic completion, ticket failure after max retries, loop completion. Generate a summary report at loop end: tickets completed, tickets failed, total iterations, duration. Future: integrate with Matrix/messaging bus when available.
acceptance_criteria: Voice notifications on key events, summary report generated at loop end, extensible for future messaging integration.

title: Loop configuration and cost control
description: Document and implement the loop-specific et config pattern. The loop config (e.g. electrictown_loop.yaml) uses cheap/local models for workers (Ollama qwen-coder), mid-tier for mayor (Big Pickle or similar), and optional cloud fallback for reviewer. Include a sample electrictown_loop.yaml in docs/. Add --cost-limit flag to cap estimated API spend per loop run.
acceptance_criteria: Sample loop config documented, cost limit flag implemented, config uses local-first model selection.

title: et loop integration tests
description: Integration tests for the loop subcommand. Test: iteration with mock bd output, retry logic, max iteration cap, epic filtering, verification gate, notification triggers. Use test fixtures for bd JSON output.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover iteration, retries, caps, filtering, verification, notifications. All pass.

title: Replace anthropic-sdk-go with native Anthropic HTTP client
description: Remove any Anthropic SDK dependency. Implement native HTTP client for Messages API with SSE streaming.

title: OpenCode CLI detection and setup
description: Implement OpenCode detection in internal/agent/adapters/opencode/detect.go. Check for 'opencode' binary, get version. OpenCode is Go-based like et - consider whether the serve mode (HTTP) could be used as an alternative transport to SSH for remote instances.
acceptance_criteria: Detection finds opencode binary, reports version, identifies serve mode availability.

title: OpenCode run mode integration
description: Implement Execute method using 'opencode run --model model task' for one-shot execution. Support -q (quiet) flag for script-friendly output. Configure provider/model via agent config flags.
acceptance_criteria: Execute works via opencode run, quiet mode supported, model configurable via config.

title: OpenCode serve mode integration
description: Implement an alternative transport using OpenCode 'opencode serve' HTTP server mode. This enables remote access without SSH - connect to a running OpenCode server via HTTP. Use 'opencode run --attach http://host:port task' for remote execution. This is a unique capability among the agent adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Serve mode transport connects to remote OpenCode server, tasks submitted via --attach, output collected.

title: OpenCode output parsing and normalization
description: Implement Normalizer for OpenCode output. Parse both standard and quiet mode output. Extract file changes, explanations, and errors.
acceptance_criteria: Normalizer handles both output modes, extracts file changes and prose.

title: OpenCode adapter tests
description: Unit tests for OpenCode adapter. Test detection, run mode, serve mode transport, output parsing, error handling.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover all modes, normalization, error cases. All pass.

title: Gemini CLI detection and auth validation
description: Implement Gemini CLI detection in internal/agent/adapters/geminicli/detect.go. Check for 'gemini' binary, get version. Validate Google auth (Gemini CLI uses Google account auth). Report free tier vs paid status.
acceptance_criteria: Detection finds gemini binary, reports version, validates auth status, identifies tier.

title: Gemini CLI --prompt mode integration
description: Implement Execute method using 'gemini -p task' for non-interactive execution. Use --output-format json for structured output. Configure via agent config flags. Handle Gemini CLI built-in tools (Google Search, file ops, shell commands).
acceptance_criteria: Execute works via -p flag, JSON output parsed, configured flags passed through.

title: Gemini CLI output parsing and normalization
description: Implement Normalizer for Gemini CLI output. Parse JSON output format to extract file changes, explanations, tool use results, and errors. Fall back to text parsing if JSON unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Normalizer handles JSON and text output, extracts file changes and prose.

title: Gemini CLI adapter tests
description: Unit tests for Gemini CLI adapter. Test detection, --prompt mode, JSON output parsing, text fallback, error handling.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover detection, execution, normalization, error cases. All pass.

Free tier with generous limits (60 req/min, 1000/day). Google direct competitor to Claude Code. Depends on Agent Backend Core (ET-96) and SSH Remote Transport (ET-104). Branch: feature/agent-gemini-cli, PR to main.
acceptance_criteria: Gemini CLI adapter implements AgentBackend, uses --prompt mode with JSON output, output normalized.

Depends on Agent Backend Core (ET-96) and SSH Remote Transport (ET-104). Branch: feature/agent-opencode, PR to main.
acceptance_criteria: OpenCode adapter implements AgentBackend, supports both run and serve modes, output normalized.

Depends on Agent Backend Core (ET-205) and SSH Remote Transport (ET-213). Branch: feature/agent-cursor, PR to main.
acceptance_criteria: Cursor adapter implements AgentBackend, works locally and via SSH, output normalized to AgentResult, configurable in agents section.

acceptance_criteria: Detection finds cursor binary, reports version, identifies available headless modes.

title: Cursor headless mode integration

acceptance_criteria: Execute sends task to Cursor in headless mode, collects output, respects timeout.

title: Cursor output parsing and normalization

title: Cursor adapter tests

acceptance_criteria: Tests cover detection, execution, normalization, error cases. All pass.

acceptance_criteria: Provider type 'groq' accepted, uses OpenAI adapter, default base_url points to Groq API.

acceptance_criteria: Provider type 'cerebras' accepted, uses OpenAI adapter, default base_url points to Cerebras API.

title: Cross-Platform Build System
description: Build system supporting cross-compilation for AMD64, ARM64, RISCV64, PPC, PPC64. Default to host architecture, with build-all option producing distributable artifacts (subdirectory or tarball per arch). Implementation approach (Makefile, shell script, etc.) determined by architect.

title: Architect cross-compilation build approach
description: Evaluate Makefile vs shell script vs Go-based build tool (mage, task, etc.) for cross-compilation. Must support: GOOS=linux with GOARCH=amd64,arm64,riscv64,ppc64,ppc64le. Consider: CGO_ENABLED=0 for static binaries, version injection via -ldflags, output naming convention (et-linux-amd64, etc.), build-all target with dist/ directory or per-arch tarballs. Recommend approach and document rationale.

title: Implement build script with single-arch default
description: Create the build script (per ET-32 decision). Must: detect host GOARCH as default, accept arch argument to override, build all binaries in cmd/ (et, et-poc, et-poc-parallel, et-poc-mixed), inject version via ldflags from git describe or git rev-parse --short HEAD, output to build/ or dist/ directory with arch-specific naming.

title: Add build-all target for all architectures
description: Add build-all option that cross-compiles for all 5 targets: linux/amd64, linux/arm64, linux/riscv64, linux/ppc64, linux/ppc64le. Output to dist/{os}-{arch}/ subdirectories with binaries, or create tarballs (dist/electrictown-linux-amd64.tar.gz etc.) suitable for copying to target hosts. Include a manifest or checksums file (sha256sums.txt).

title: Test cross-compilation for all target architectures
description: Verify that go build succeeds for all 5 GOARCH targets (amd64, arm64, riscv64, ppc64, ppc64le) with CGO_ENABLED=0. Verify file type with 'file' command on each binary. Verify version string injection. This is a compilation check, not a runtime test (we may not have hardware for all arches).

title: Project Documentation and GitHub Presence

Credit original inspirations (gastown by Steve Yegge, LiteLLM) while explaining how electrictown has diverged into its own implementation. Include architecture overview, quickstart, configuration reference, and build instructions.

title: Write GitHub repository description
description: Set the short GitHub repo description (About section). Should concisely convey: provider-agnostic multi-agent coding orchestrator in Go, routes any LLM provider (Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini) through a unified router with role-based model assignment, fallback chains, and cost tracking. Keep under 350 chars (GitHub limit). Also set relevant topics/tags.

title: Write comprehensive README.md

title: Ollama Authentication Support
description: Add comprehensive optional authentication support for Ollama instances. Local Ollama requires no auth (default). Ollama Cloud uses Bearer token (Authorization: Bearer API_KEY). Self-hosted network Ollama behind reverse proxies may use Bearer tokens or HTTP Basic Auth. Our adapter already sends Bearer when api_key is set, but needs config ergonomics, Basic Auth support for proxied instances, and documentation.

title: Dependency Replacement - Self-Contained Goal
description: Track and plan replacement of all 3rd party libraries with native Go implementations. PoC uses external libs (go-openai, ollama/api, etc.) but medium-term goal is self-contained with only provider SDKs as external deps. Each task represents one library to internalize.

title: Add auth_type field to ProviderConfig for Ollama
description: Add an optional auth_type field to ProviderConfig (YAML: auth_type) supporting: 'bearer' (default when api_key set), 'basic' (HTTP Basic Auth for reverse-proxied Ollama), 'none' (explicit no-auth, default when no api_key). For 'basic' auth, api_key field holds 'username:password' which gets base64-encoded into 'Authorization: Basic ...' header. This is provider-agnostic in the config but initially used by the Ollama adapter for proxied instances. Other providers always use their native auth.

title: Update Ollama adapter to support Bearer and Basic auth
description: Update internal/provider/ollama/ollama.go setHeaders() to read auth_type from config. Currently hardcodes Bearer. Should support: (1) no api_key → no auth header (local default), (2) api_key with auth_type=bearer or unset → Authorization: Bearer (Ollama Cloud, Bearer-proxy), (3) api_key='user:pass' with auth_type=basic → Authorization: Basic base64(user:pass) (nginx/Caddy proxied Ollama). The New() constructor needs to accept the auth_type, either as a new parameter or via an Option. Add tests for all three auth paths.

title: Update Ollama factory to pass auth_type from config
description: Update the Ollama provider factory in cmd/et/main.go buildFactories() to pass pc.AuthType (or equivalent) to the Ollama constructor. Currently only passes baseURL and apiKey. Ensure the factory correctly wires auth_type from YAML config through ProviderConfig to the Ollama adapter.

title: Add config validation for auth_type values
description: Validate auth_type in Config.Validate(): must be empty (default), 'bearer', 'basic', or 'none'. If auth_type=basic and api_key doesn't contain ':', warn or error. If auth_type=bearer or basic but api_key is empty, error. If auth_type=none but api_key is set, warn (auth_type=none with a key is suspicious). Add tests for all validation cases.

title: Document Ollama auth configuration in README
description: Add an 'Authentication' subsection to the Ollama section of README.md covering: (1) Local Ollama — no auth needed (default), (2) Ollama Cloud — set api_key to your Ollama API key, uses Bearer automatically, (3) Proxied Ollama with Bearer — same as cloud, set api_key, (4) Proxied Ollama with Basic Auth — set auth_type: basic and api_key: 'user:pass'. Include YAML config examples for each scenario. Reference Ollama's official docs at docs.ollama.com/api/authentication.

title: Document Caddy reverse proxy setup for Ollama
description: Create docs/caddy-reverse-proxy.md covering Caddy as a reverse proxy in front of Ollama for network deployments. Include: (1) Why — secure Ollama for network/multi-host access with TLS and auth, (2) Caddy install, (3) Basic Caddyfile config proxying to localhost:11434 with automatic HTTPS via Let's Encrypt, (4) Adding Basic Auth (caddy hash-password), (5) Adding Bearer token auth via header matching, (6) Example electrictown.yaml configs for each auth scenario, (7) TLS section strongly encouraging HTTPS with links to Let's Encrypt docs (https://letsencrypt.org/docs/) and Caddy's automatic HTTPS docs (https://caddyserver.com/docs/automatic-https), (8) Troubleshooting common issues. Link from README.md's Ollama auth section. Separate .md file, not inline in README.
